newsitem.title: FRANCE: French corporate earnings forecasts revised down.
newsitem.headline: French corporate earnings forecasts revised down.

text.p: French corporate earnings forecasts were revised down 5.4 percent during the third quarter for 150 companies which have issued half-year results, consulting firm Jacques Chahine Finance said on Monday.
The companies represent two-thirds of the Paris bourse's capitalisation.

Forecasts were revised down 3.7 percent for the 31 companies making up the blue chip CAC 40 index that have issued their results, said Jacques Chahine Finance, which surveyed 75 French and foreign brokers.

For 1996, French companies representing 99 percent of the bourse's capitalisation are expected to report combined profits of 143 billion francs, compared with 68 billion for 1995 and 96 billion for the previous year, it said.
The "real-time" survey incorporates estimates updated to reflect first-half results.

"The financial sector published better than expected results, creating the biggest positive surprise for the market. Despite signs of recovery, the financial sector trails the market," the consulting firm said in a statement.
"Forecasts for the energy sector have also been revised up. In contrast, earnings for the automotive, public works and raw materials sectors were below market expectations," it said.
"Based on 66 percent of the capitalisation having reported results, the median growth of these companies comes to 13.1 percent from 14.9 percent expected," it said.
Combined profits for the CAC 40 components are estimated at 82 billion francs for 1996, compared with 28 billion in 1995 and 68 billion in 1994.
"This results in 1996 price-earnings ratios of 19.6 and 20.1 for the CAC-40," it said.
"For the 1997 the PE ratios are 15.8 and 16.5 respectively."
